features.text: The patient has had knee pain for about six months.
The knee pain has been worsening, especially when getting up from sitting or going up and down stairs.
The knee pain is located behind the kneecaps and affects both sides of the knee.
The patient has not experienced swelling, stiffness, or locking of the knee.
The patient does not recall any prior injuries or surgeries to the knee.
The patient has not undergone any imaging studies or blood tests for knee pain.
The patient works from home and is at a desk most of the day.
The patient used to run 5 to 6 miles a day but now can barely run half a mile due to knee pain.
The patient does not have any family history of joint-related conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, or lupus.
The patient has not experienced morning stiffness, fatigue, fever, or weight loss.
The patient has noticed creaking sounds in the knees during movement.
The patient has not experienced episodes of the knee giving way or locking.
The patient has not experienced numbness, tingling, or weakness in the legs.
The knee pain worsens when getting up from a seated position, after watching TV, or when going up and down stairs.
The knee pain feels better when resting, but the patient cannot stretch much due to pain.
The patient has not undergone any imaging studies such as X-rays, MRI, or ultrasound of the knees in the past.
The patient has not undergone any blood tests to evaluate for inflammatory or autoimmune conditions.
